newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance up despite likely fall in profit.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance up despite likely fall in profit.

text.p: Shares of India's largest private firm Reliance Industries Ltd rose across major bourses on Monday despite widespread expectations that it will report lower net profit for financial 96/97 (April-March).
Reliance, among the most actively traded shares on Indian stockmarkets, was quoted at 299.30 rupees, up 19.05 rupees, on the National Stock Exchange.
Reliance crossed the 300-rupee mark on the Bombay Stock Exchange, touching 307.75 rupees in late afternoon trade on Monday, up 27.75 rupees from the previous close.
The Reliance board will meet on Tuesday to finalise results.
"This year's results will not matter much," said Tridib Pathak, senior analyst at UBS Securities.
He said the market was looking ahead as Reliance's massive new expansion projects come bear fruits in the new year.
A Reuters poll of 28 securities firms on Monday showed Reliance would post a net profit of 12.06 billion rupees for 1996/97, recording a 7.63 percent fall over the same period a year ago.
"We are forecasting a net profit of 12.81 billion rupees," said Shoma Roy, an analyst at Daewoo Securities.
She expected operating margins to fall to 30.9 percent during the year from 35.0 percent in 1995/96.
"Basically the Reliance story is their expansion is more or less complete. The cracker has been commissioned. They will get benefit of integration of operations from FY1998," Roy said.
"Reliance now looks better than IPCL," she said, referring to the state-run Indian Petrochemicals Corp.
Its 1996/97 results would have been much worse but for new capacities in polyester and polypropylene, analysts said.
Reliance commissioned a 350,000 tonne-per-year polypropylene plant and raised its polyester yarn capacity by another 60,000 tonnes during 1996/97.

Prices of polyester and polymers -- Reliance's bread and butter -- fell sharply during the year but capacity increases would help Reliance show a post-tax profit not too sharply different from the previous year, analysts said.

Payment of corporate taxes for the first time in Reliance's history -- Reliance paid 500 million rupees in advance tax on March 15 -- following a minimum alternate tax announced in the 1996/97 (April-March) budget would also pull down the firm's results, analysts said.
"This year's profit has been discounted by the market," said a petrochemical analyst at an international brokerage in Bombay.
"Reliance FY97 and FY98 are almost like two companies in terms of capacities," he said.

He said Reliance's polyester yarn capacity jumped by 125 percent, polyester fibre capacity by 177 percent and polyester input PTA (purified terephthalic acid) capacity by 140 percent, most of it towards the close of financial year 1996/97.
But one analyst asked whether Reliance would be able to dispose of all its new production.
"Outook for the new year is positive, but where will they sell all the fibre and yarn?" asked an analyst who said he expected excess capacity to emerge later this year.
